title: Cells and tissues may have something it is like to make decisions

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cells and tissues may have something it is like to make decisions

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because some nervous systems give rise to first-person experience and neural and non-neural networks differ minimally apart from time scale, it is natural to hypothesize that there is something it is like to be a tissue or organ making decisions, e.g. a pancreas may have as much proto-consciousness as a simple neural network.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › What Does It Feel Like to be a Pancreas?

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But, given that at least some nervous systems do give rise to such experience and that the differences between neural networks and non-neural ones (aside from temporal scale) are minimal, it is natural to hypothesize that there is something-it-is-like to being a tissue or organ and making decisions.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “What Does It Feel Like to be a Pancreas?”. Scope: Non-neural tissues and organs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-30: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.05

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim's central content is phenomenal rather than behavioral. Existing tissue recordings can characterize decision-like dynamics but cannot resolve whether there is something it is like to instantiate them.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No behavioral, physiological, or computational measurement can presently distinguish a tissue that has first-person experience from one with identical functions but no experience.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
First-person experience in non-reporting tissue has no agreed observable marker.

Functional similarity does not discriminate phenomenal experience from its absence.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.1
data adequacy: 0.02
operationalizability: 0.05
discriminating power: 0.02
data existence: 0.05

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The hypothesis is about first-person experience in non-neural organs. Neural and physiological data can describe decision-like dynamics, and those same records remain compatible with or without proto-consciousness. Nothing in current public data supplies a confirming or refuting observation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No third-person variable would be present if a tissue had experience while deciding and absent if the same tissue only carried out the same physiological dynamics.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Phenomenal 'something it is like' has no public measurement that separates it from the physiological description of the same events.
